title: Malaria and human history
summary: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites passed between people by female Anopheles mosquitoes. One species, Plasmodium falciparum, is thought to have become a major human pathogen within the past 5,000 to 10,000 years, as farming took root in western and central Africa and changed the human environment. Human genetic traits that protect against malaria, such as sickle cell trait, were selected in response. In 2024 malaria caused an estimated 610,000 deaths, 95% of them in the WHO African Region.
